title: Transient quota reconciliation bug triggers cascading fallback and degraded responses for Dedicated customers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A subset of Dedicated tenants experienced degraded API responses (increased 5xx and 429s) over a 3‑hour window due to a quota reconciliation race between the per-tenant quota service and the burst allowance updater. The reconciliation produced transient negative available-burst values for some tenants, which triggered our fallback router to take requests offline to a lower-tier model variant. The fallback loop then exhausted a secondary rate bucket and produced cascading 503/429s for affected customers.

Scope & Impact:
- Affected deployments: Dedicated clusters in us-west-2 (customers on older Dedicated agent versions).
- Customer impact: 4 paying customers saw elevated error rates and request latency spikes; 2 customers reported partial outages and opened support escalations (Acme Analytics, FinSight).
- Time window: 2026-02-09 22:14 UTC – 2026-02-10 01:26 UTC (mitigation began at 22:30 UTC; full stable state at 01:26 UTC after config rollouts).
- SLOs: latency and error SLOs violated for ~2.8 hours for affected tenants.

Root Cause (summary):
An edge case in the quota reconciliation routine caused the per-tenant burst allowance to be decremented twice during a near-simultaneous update: 1) scheduled quota refresh job and 2) an on-demand quota refresh triggered by a reallocation event. The code path lacked idempotency for the burst token bookkeeping when concurrent updates raced, which allowed the stored burst allowance to go negative. Our routing layer treats negative available burst as a signal to fallback immediately to a lower-capacity serving plane. Because the lower-capacity plane had much tighter local bucket limits per instance, it quickly hit its quota and returned 503/429s, creating a feedback loop back into the reconciliation logic as clients retried.

Why this was not caught earlier:
- The invariant (burst allowance must never be negative) was implied but not asserted in unit tests.
- Intermittency: the race requires a specific timing of scheduler and an on-demand refresh, frequent only under certain autoscaling churn seen on older Dedicated agent versions.
- Existing monitoring surfaced elevated 5xxs but not the negative-burst-state metric until we extended logs during the incident.

Repro steps (dev environment):
1) Deploy a Dedicated cluster with agent v1.9.3 and enable scheduled quota refresh every 30s.
2) Create a tenant with a small burst allowance and high request rate.
3) Simultaneously trigger an on-demand quota refresh via the admin API while the scheduled job runs (use two processes to narrow the timing).
4) Observe stored burst_allowance dropping below zero and routing decision switching to fallback low-capacity plane.

Mitigation (what we did during incident):
- 22:30 UTC: Disabled scheduled quota refresh window across affected Dedicated clusters to stop concurrent updates.
- 22:44 UTC: Manually reconciled negative burst values for top 4 impacted tenants.
- 23:10 UTC: Rolled a hotfix to routing layer to treat negative burst allowance as zero (safeguard) and added telemetry to emit an alert on negative values.
- 00:05 UTC: Rolled config change to increase secondary-plane local bucket sizes to absorb transient traffic while full fix prepared.

Permanent fix implemented in this ticket (summary):
- Add compare-and-swap (CAS) based update path to quota reconciliation to ensure idempotent updates to burst_allowance.
- Add database-level check constraint to reject negative burst values (defense in depth).
- Add unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent refreshes and assert burst_allowance >= 0.
- Emit a new metric tenant.quota.burst_negative_count and an alert threshold to catch regressions early.

Deployment & rollout plan:
- Branch: github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-quota/compare/ENG-23618-burst-cas
- Staged rollout: canary on one Dedicated cluster (us-east-1) -> gradual rollout across Dedicated clusters over 24h with monitor gates.
- Rollback plan: revert to previous quota-service binary; immediately re-enable scheduled refresh if we observe repeat regression.

Post-incident actions and follow-ups (owners):
- (Action) Add assert and test coverage for burst invariants — owner: Marco Hernandez — ETA: 2026-02-18.
- (Action) Update Dedicated agent upgrade doc to recommend v1.10.0+ for clusters with high autoscale churn — owner: Emily Nguyen — ETA: 2026-02-20.
- (Action) Add runbook to respond to negative burst alerts with automated reconcile tool — owner: SRE team (Dani Liu) — ETA: 2026-02-25.
- (Action) Customer communication follow-up and credits for impacted tenants — owner: Customer Success (Ravi Kapoor) — ETA: 2026-02-17.

Artifacts & links:
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-quota/pull/324 (fix + CAS updates)
- Hotfix rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/198
- Incident timeline pulse: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-02-10+-+Dedicated+quota+reconciliation
- Alert dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quotas/tenant-burst

Notes about Hosted & Private:
- Hosted: the hosted control plane was not affected because it uses a different refresh cadence and additional optimistic locking. We reviewed the hosted code path to confirm guardrails are sufficient.
- Private/VPC: Private deployments running versions older than 1.10.0 are vulnerable; recommend customers using Private to upgrade to the patched runtime or apply the runtime guard. We'll include this vulnerability note in the Private advisory.
